checkpoints.title: Tradeoff duel
checkpoints.prompt: You add a node to a 10-node cache. What happens to the keys?

options.label: Hash modulo node count
options.verdict: One extra node changes N, so nearly every key maps somewhere new and roughly 90% of the cache is invalidated at once. The resulting stampede onto the origin is how cache expansions take down databases.

options.label: Consistent hashing with virtual nodes
options.verdict: Only the keys between the new node and its predecessor move — about 1/N of them. Virtual nodes keep the split even so one physical node does not inherit a disproportionate arc.

defend.prompt: Why virtual nodes rather than one point per server?

options.label: A few random points distribute unevenly
They let heterogeneous servers own different shares
Removing a node spreads its load across many peers
They reduce the number of keys that move on a change

defend.explain: The fraction that moves is ~1/N either way. Virtual nodes fix distribution, not volume: even balance, weighted capacity, and a failure that spreads across the ring instead of landing entirely on one neighbour.

checkpoints.title: Capacity ladder
checkpoints.prompt: Growing a cache tier from MVP to serious load.

rungs.q: Where a single Redis node stops being enough
rungs.note: One node handles six figures comfortably; past that you shard.

rungs.q: Keys displaced when adding one node to N
rungs.note: The entire reason consistent hashing exists.

rungs.q: What a cache miss storm threatens
rungs.note: The cache is fine — it is the thing behind it that falls over.

checkpoints.explain: Cache design is mostly about protecting what sits behind the cache. Every choice here is judged by what happens on a miss.

checkpoints.title: Architecture builder
checkpoints.prompt: Build the read path with a miss.
checkpoints.explain: The ring picks the node; on a miss the coalescer sits between the cache and the origin so a thousand concurrent misses for one key become a single origin read. Without it, a hot key expiring is a thousand simultaneous queries.

checkpoints.title: Spot the bottleneck
checkpoints.prompt: p99 latency tripled after adding three nodes to the ring.
checkpoints.explain: One node's hit rate collapsed while its peers barely moved — that is not a general cold-cache effect, it is uneven redistribution. Node B inherited a large arc of the ring, probably because it was added with too few virtual nodes, so it holds a disproportionate share of keys it has never seen. The origin latency is that node's misses arriving downstream.

wrong.Origin Database: It is absorbing the misses. Ask which node is generating them.
wrong.Request Coalescer: 88% dedup means it is working; it can only collapse duplicates, not manufacture hits.
wrong.Cache Node A: Down 2 points is normal churn after a topology change.
